Fit a linear mixed model

Source: R/fit.R
vlm_fit.Rd

Fits the linear mixed model \(\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{Z}\mathbf{u} + \mathbf{e}\) by restricted maximum likelihood (REML), maximum likelihood (ML) or the method of moments on Type 3 mean squares, and gives the results of SAS PROC MIXED: covariance parameter estimates with standard errors, the solution for the fixed effects in the overparameterised coding, Type 3 (or Type 1) tests with containment, residual, between-within, Satterthwaite or Kenward-Roger denominator degrees of freedom, and fit statistics. It is the engine behind every analysis of the book of Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998).

Usage

vlm_fit(
  fixed,
  data,
  random = NULL,
  repeated = NULL,
  method = c("REML", "ML", "Type3"),
  ddfm = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr"),
  type = 3,
  class = NULL,
  bound = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

# Default S3 method
vlm_fit(
  fixed,
  data,
  random = NULL,
  repeated = NULL,
  method = c("REML", "ML", "Type3"),
  ddfm = c("default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth", "kr"),
  type = 3,
  class = NULL,
  bound = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

fixed

two-sided formula of the response and the fixed effects, such as Pcv ~ Drug * dose; terms are kept in the order written, as in a SAS MODEL statement (a/b gives a + a:b).

data

a data frame (or data.table) with the variables.

random

NULL, a one-sided formula of random variance components (each term one component, such as ~ Region + Region:Drug), a vlm_random() specification, or a list of these.

repeated

NULL or a vlm_repeated() specification of the residual covariance.

method

"REML" (default), "ML" or "Type3".

ddfm

denominator degrees of freedom: "default", "contain", "residual", "betwithin", "satterth" or "kr", the DDFM= keywords of SAS.

type

type of the tests of fixed effects: 3 (default) or 1 (sequential).

class

optional character vector of numeric variables to treat as classification variables (factors), like the SAS CLASS statement. Non-numeric variables and the variables of random effects and subjects are always classification variables.

bound

logical; keep variance estimates non-negative (default TRUE; FALSE is the SAS NOBOUND option).

control

list with maxit (default 200), tol (default \(10^{-12}\)) and start (starting values of the covariance parameters, in the order of the covariance table).

Value

A list of class c("vlm_fit", "vlm_result", "list") with covariance (covariance parameter estimates, standard errors and Wald Z tests), fixed (solution for the fixed effects), tests (tests of the fixed effects), fit (fit statistics) and dimensions; the call is kept in attr(, "call"). Further analyses of the fit: vlm_lsmeans(), vlm_estimate(), vlm_contrast(), vlm_blup(), vlm_compare() and vlm_interpret().

Details

With \(\mathbf{u} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{G})\) and \(\mathbf{e} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{R})\) independent, \(\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{Z}\mathbf{G}\mathbf{Z}^{\top} + \mathbf{R}\) depends on the covariance parameters \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\). With \(P = \mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{X})\) and \(N\) observations, the REML log-likelihood is $$\ell_R(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = -\frac{1}{2}\left\{(N - P)\log(2\pi) + \log|\mathbf{V}| + \log|\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{X}| + \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{r}\right\},$$ with \(\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}\); the ML log-likelihood drops the third term and uses \(N\) in the first. It is maximised by Newton steps with the average-information matrix \(\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{y}^{\top}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}_i\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}_j\mathbf{P}\mathbf{y}\), where \(\mathbf{V}_i = \partial\mathbf{V}/\partial\theta_i\) and \(\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{V}^{-1} - \mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{X})^{-}\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1}\), with step halving and variances kept non-negative (unless bound = FALSE). The fixed effects are the generalised least-squares solution $$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = (\mathbf{X}^{\top}\widehat{\mathbf{V}}^{-1}\mathbf{X})^{-} \mathbf{X}^{\top}\widehat{\mathbf{V}}^{-1}\mathbf{y}$$ in the overparameterised coding (one column per level), with the generalised inverse that sets aliased levels to zero, as SAS does. Standard errors of the covariance parameters come from the observed information.

Type 3 tests use the sum-to-zero coding of each effect (the SAS Type 3 hypothesis when every cell is observed). The denominator degrees of freedom (ddfm) are: "contain", the rank contribution of the random effects that contain the fixed effect, or \(N - \mathrm{rank}[\mathbf{X}\ \mathbf{Z}]\) if none does; "residual", \(N - \mathrm{rank}[\mathbf{X}\ \mathbf{Z}]\); "betwithin", the between- and within-subject parts of the residual degrees of freedom; "satterth", \(\nu = 2\{\mathbf{l}^{\top}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{l}\}^2 / \mathbf{g}^{\top}\mathbf{A}\mathbf{g}\), with \(\mathbf{g}\) the gradient of \(\mathbf{l}^{\top}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{l}\) in \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\) and \(\mathbf{A}\) the asymptotic covariance of \(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\) (Giesbrecht and Burns 1985; Fai and Cornelius 1996 for several rows); "kr", the adjusted covariance and scaled F of Kenward and Roger (1997). "default" chooses as SAS: containment with random effects, between-within with a residual structure only, residual otherwise.

Method "Type3" (random variance components only) equates the Type 3 mean squares of the random effects to their expectations (vlm_ems()); negative solutions are set to zero.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi.

Patterson, H. D. and Thompson, R. (1971). Recovery of inter-block information when block sizes are unequal. Biometrika, 58, 545-554.

Kenward, M. G. and Roger, J. H. (1997). Small sample inference for fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics, 53, 983-997.

See also

vlm_random, vlm_lsmeans, vlm_estimate, vlm_ems

Other VetResearchLMM models: vlm_compare(), vlm_ems(), vlm_random()

Examples

# Example 2.5.1.1: PROC MIXED; CLASS drug dose region; MODEL pcv = drug dose drug*dose / SOLUTION;
# RANDOM region drug*region;
fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
fm
#> Linear mixed model: Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
#> Estimation: REML; denominator df: satterth; converged after 6 iterations
#> Random: Region; Region:Drug
#> 
#> Covariance parameter estimates
#>    parameter subject estimate     se      z      p
#>       Region            5.151  3.739  1.378 0.0842

#>     Residual            2.096 0.9375  2.236 0.0127
#> 
#> Fit statistics
#>                 statistic   value
#>     -2 Res Log Likelihood 92.3786
#>   AIC (smaller is better) 98.3786
#>  AICC (smaller is better) 99.8786
#>   BIC (smaller is better) 101.366
#>

# Example 3.3, Model 2: first-order autoregressive residuals within an animal
ar <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = PCV ~ breed + breed:time
    , data     = ex33
    , random   = NULL
    , repeated = vlm_repeated(
          type    = c("vc", "cs", "ar1", "sp_pow", "un")[3]
        , subject = ~ animal_id:breed
        , order   = ~ time
        )
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
ar$covariance
#>    parameter         subject  estimate         se        z            p
#>       <char>          <char>     <num>      <num>    <num>        <num>
